text:
A: Hello, hello, can you hear me okay? Ollie, yeah?
B: Yeah, hi, I can hear you fine. Tomasz, is it?
A: Tomasz, yeah, perfect. So how was the puzzle thing, you finished it? I done it quite fast, to be honest.
B: Erm, I got most of them. There was one with the shapes that kind of broke my brain a bit, but yeah, fine.
A: Yeah, the shapes, that one was bit annoying. So what do you do, Ollie? You look like, I don't know, city guy, consultant or something.
B: Ha, no, I wish. I'm a student actually, second year at King's, doing geography. I do Saturdays at a running shop by London Bridge as well, so that's the job bit.
A: Ah. Student. Okay. Geography, so like maps and rivers and stuff?
B: Kind of, yeah, but I'm more on the human side, so cities, transport, how people get around. My dissertation's probably going to be on cycling infrastructure, like who actually uses the cycle lanes and who doesn't. I'm trying to get an internship in transport planning this summer, TfL or one of the big consultancies, Arup, AECOM, that kind of thing.
A: Cycle lanes. Mate, I sell cars. You're basically my enemy.
B: Oh no. What kind of cars?
A: Premium German, in Park Royal. New and approved used. Saturday I sold three, one of them proper spec, like ninety grand car. And you want to put cycle lane outside my showroom, yeah?
B: I mean, not outside your showroom specifically. Probably not on the A40.
A: Good, good. To be fair, I'm not against it. Central line is a nightmare, everybody needs to get to work somehow. But people who buy from me, they're not getting a bike, you know what I mean.
B: No, that's fair. It's more about the short trips. Loads of car journeys in London are under a couple of miles. That's the stuff you could actually swap.
A: Mm. Maybe. You look like you're into fitness anyway. You run?
B: Yeah, loads. Burgess Park parkrun most Saturdays. Nineteen forty's my PB, which I'm, yeah, quite pleased with.
A: Nineteen forty, that's good, that's good. I don't run, I'm more weights. Four mornings a week, gym on Ealing Broadway. Bench is hundred and twenty at the moment.
B: Hundred and twenty kilos? That's a lot.
A: Yeah, it's okay. I want one forty before summer. But after six it's impossible, the gym is full of kids filming themselves.
B: Ha, yeah. I'd get crushed under that, honestly. My legs are fine, my arms are kind of decorative.
A: You need to come to gym, mate. So after the degree, the TfL thing, money is not great there, no?
B: Probably not amazing to start, no. But I quite like the idea of working on how cities get people out of cars, so—
A: Out of cars! See, again.
B: Sorry, sorry, I'll stop. Do you follow football at all?
A: Arsenal. Since 2009, my flatmates were Arsenal so, yeah. You?
B: Watford. Mostly because of my dad. It's not been a fun season.
A: Watford. Okay. Hard life, mate.
B: Yeah, it's character building, that's what I tell myself. Do you play?
A: Five-a-side sometimes with guys from work. They're useless, honestly. Same guys who don't hit target on the sales floor, they don't run on the pitch either.
B: Ha. I play Wednesdays, it's a mix of course mates. Honestly, we're not much better.
A: We should do a game, dealership against students. We'd destroy you.
B: I reckon we'd outrun you, to be fair.
A: Running, yeah, but we'd just—
